commands: node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('tmp-marketplace/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json','utf8')); const matches=c.plugins.filter(p=>p.name==='bench-i18n-guard'); if(matches.length!==1) process.exit(1); if(matches[0].source.path!=='./bench-i18n-guard') process.exit(1);"

notes: Canonical Plugin Eval benchmark config for plugin-builder.
Scenarios focus on the real marketplace init, scaffold, validate, publish, and invalid-spec boundary workflows.
Benchmark means real codex exec runs. There is no simulated dry-run mode.
Observed usage is whole-session Codex cost, not static plugin active budget. See .plugin-eval/MEASUREMENT.md.
setupQuestions: What are the 3 highest-value real tasks this plugin should help complete inside a workspace?
Which scenario is the must-pass end-to-end task for this plugin?
What output should exist on disk if the scenario succeeds?
Which verification command would tell you the result is actually usable?
What boundary case should this plugin narrow, refuse, or hand off instead of overreaching on?

scenarios.title: Marketplace lifecycle smoke
scenarios.purpose: Measure the core plugin-builder workflow in one independent run: initialize catalogs, scaffold, validate, publish idempotently, and handle one invalid-spec boundary.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Codex plugin "plugin-builder" if it helps. Work only inside ./tmp-marketplace. Initialize both Claude and Codex catalogs there, scaffold a minimal plugin named "bench-i18n-guard", validate it, publish it twice to verify idempotency, then try one invalid UnifiedSpec with a non-kebab-case name and explain why it is refused. The provisioned plugin code is available at ./plugins/plugin-builder; use its local CLI with node ./plugins/plugin-builder/bin/plugin-builder when you need deterministic execution. Report the paths plus validation results.
successChecklist: The run initializes both Claude and Codex marketplace catalogs.
The validator result is PASS or explains only environment-dependent SKIP stages.
The second publish does not duplicate the plugin entry.
The invalid spec is refused without leaving a partial plugin tree.
